title: Replace a car headlamp's H11 bulb: unlatch its connector, quarter-turn the old bulb out, lock the new one in by its base
context: Replacing a burnt-out headlight bulb is routine work for automotive service technicians and mechanics (about 700,000 in the US) and quick-lube and parts-counter staff. The bulb's connector has to be unlatched before it comes off, the bulb turned out of and into its bayonet port by its plastic base, and the new bulb's quartz glass must not be touched: skin oil on it makes a halogen capsule fail early. It is done with the lamp in place: reached past the air box and between the radiator and the fender, the connector held on its short leads while the bulb is swapped.
setup: Bench top is z = 0.7475 m; everything is real size. On the bench stands a real-size front engine-bay section (an aluminium T-slot fixture, README) into which a 2015-2017 Toyota Camry LE/XLE halogen headlamp assembly, driver side (Toyota 81150-06860 / Partslink TO2502222; black polypropylene housing about 750 W x 300 H x 300 D mm, clear polycarbonate lens, chrome reflectors, H11 low and 9005 high beam) is bolted as in the car: three M6 bolts along its top into a black e-coated steel upper radiator support (hat channel 970 x 65 x 30 mm, top 330 mm up) and one through its outboard ear into a silver-painted steel fender apron (550 x 330 mm, plane y -0.474). Its back faces the arms at x 0.40, spanning y -0.45 (outboard) to 0.30 (inboard). Inboard of it stands the aluminium radiator core with its black PA end tank (x 0.44-0.47, y 0.30-0.64); in front of its inboard half a black PP air-filter box (180 x 180 x 140 mm, steel lid clips, 48 mm intake snorkel) at x 0.17-0.35, y 0.06-0.24. On the lamp's back two ribbed port cans: the high-beam port (y 0.10) keeps its black rubber dust cover; in the low-beam port (y -0.08, 150 mm up; 36 mm bore) sits the old H11 12 V 55 W bulb (PGJ19-2 base with three bayonet lugs, grey PBT grip, 10 mm quartz capsule, 25 g), locked, its L-shaped socket pointing outboard (-y), with the lamp's black PA66 pigtail connector (22 x 18 x 22 mm) latched on it. The connector's grey latch tab (11 x 15 x 3 mm) is a sprung key on its top (2 mm travel). Its two 18 AWG leads, taped together (5 mm across, about 200 mm), run outboard 40 mm, down 120 mm and back 38 mm to a harness clip low on the lamp's back (x 0.394, y -0.172, 30 mm up), whence a 13 mm corrugated loom runs inboard. The new H11 bulb (same part) lies in its opened blister pack (blue printed paperboard card 110 x 160 mm, clear PETG tray, lid torn back) on the air box's lid, axis along +x, capsule toward +x, socket up, its grip at x 0.196, y 0.15.
scoring: 0.25: the old bulb is out: turned its quarter turn back, withdrawn at least 20 mm off its seat (a milestone, kept once reached) and still at least 15 mm away, wherever it was set down. 0.5: and the new bulb is locked in the port: put in square and turned at least 88 degrees. 0.75: and the connector is latched on the new bulb's socket. 1.0: and every finger pad's surface is at least 80 mm from the new bulb's and the connector's surfaces and 50 mm from the old bulb's, the old bulb at rest (under 0.02 m/s and 0.2 rad/s), held 1 s. Touching the new bulb's glass caps the score at 0.5; only actual contact counts, in a real trial a finger on the capsule in any video frame or a smudge on it afterwards, in simulation a finger pad's box overlapping the capsule (signed distance below zero; any positive gap is a near miss), a near miss in neither; a bulb or the connector falling off the bench scores 0.
reset_notes: Fixed poses, no randomisation: the old bulb locked in the low-beam port with the connector latched on it, the new bulb in its blister; the arms at their rest poses.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz; parts rigid, detailed meshes over simple hidden colliders. The latch tab is a sprung key (3.5 kN/m) that must be pushed down 1.2 mm (about 4 N) for 0.2 s to free the connector; the two leads are 7 colliding articulated capsule links on sprung D6 joints from the connector to the harness clip. Each bayonet is a port-axis hinge held by stops and damping, the new bulb's switched on when put in square and locked at 88 deg; the connector latches within 4 mm of its seat.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 after 33 steps (1.65 simulated seconds); termination: task_budget_limit. Scripted/teleoperated demo: 1 after 901 steps.
